newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-MARK WAUGH LIFTS AUSTRALIA WITH FLUENT 95.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-MARK WAUGH LIFTS AUSTRALIA WITH FLUENT 95.

text.p: Mark Waugh stroked 95 from 96 balls as Australia battled to avoid a series whitewash by England in the third and final one-day international at Lord's on Sunday.

Opener Waugh propped up an uneven batting performnce by the touring team which produced 269 all out in 49.2 of their 50 overs against a buoyant England side who won each of the first two matches by six wickets.

The elegant New South Wales batsman drove and cut fluently, reaching his half-century in exactly 50 deliveries and hitting 12 fours altogether before he was trapped leg before by Darren Gough in the 33rd over.

Gough had given England the early initiative by dispatching one-day international debutant Matthew Elliott (1), acting captain Steve Waugh (17) and the prolific Michael Bevan (8)in a six-over new-ball spell that brought him three for 27.

The Yorkshire paceman removed Elliott, opening because out-of-form skipper Mark Taylor dropped himself, with the last ball of the first over, but the Waugh twins repaired the damage by adding 50 in seven overs.

Gough then had Steve Waugh brilliantly caught by Graham Thorpe, diving full length to his right at slip, and in his next over removed the dangerous Bevan who came into the match with an average of 57.69 from his previous 58 limited overs interntionals.

Mark Waugh found his most effective ally in Justin Langer (29), the pair adding 79 for the fourth wicket, with paceman Chris Silverwood consistently being punished to the tune of 44 runs in two spells of three overs.

After Waugh's departure five short of what would have been his 11th one-day international hundred, Australia had to rely on some firm blows from Adam Gilchrist (33), Ian Healy (27) and Mike Kasprowicz (28 not out) to reach a relatively competitive total.

Gough, whose consistently controlled bowling has been a key element of England's success in the series, added the wicket of Jason Gillespie in his last spell to equal his best figures in limited overs games for his country of five for 44.
